interactions.title: Alden’s love of the house and dandelions
lines: DM: Well, tomorrow we'll get to Dandelion House. And, as he says it, his demeanor changes a little bit. You can see him just light up. It's clear that he loves this place. He says, I'm so excited for you to see it, it's… gorgeous. It has everything that a manor house should.

DM: And… it's a little old, it's a little rundown. Sure, it needs a little bit of love, of course, and… and care, but it's… it's beautiful, it's exactly what it is, it's exactly what it should be. The walls, the… Cellars! The halls…
DM: Once… once… Lord Hulda just spruces it up a little bit and really moves in, it's gonna be just the thing, filled with people and life and laughter, which it isn't really now, but it will be soon.
Ayveen: Have you already started identifying artisans who'll help with the repairs once we've cleared it for safety?

DM: No, I think he's taking things one thing at a time. But I have… a big, big family in this area, and I have all sorts of cousins who can do all sorts of things, and I'm… I'm sure all of us will… will help out and put it all back together again. So… so I'm… I'm not too worried, but he's…

DM: I don't know if I've told you quite all the detail. I should leave most of them for him to say, but… There's a… There's a condition of this inheritance that… that he hasn't quite fulfilled yet, and… and that's an… I'll… I'll let him tell you about all of this when… when we get there.
Ayveen: Will we be meeting them in the house or outside before we arrive?
DM: No, when we get… when we get to the grounds, if we push hard tomorrow, I think we'll get there. I'm excited for you to see it.
DM: And he grins and falls silent.
Tarek: I heard… Rhododendron house is actually nicer.
DM: You… I… hmm… hmm… So, Alden.

DM: From a single dandelion can travel hundreds of miles… and that… the same dandelions that grow on the west side of the mountains grow on the east. What greater traveler is there than a seed? It's remarkable. Hmm.

DM: Have you ever seen, at dawn and dusk, in a field of dandelions, if you blow, the way the light shines on each of them, it's one of the most beautiful things I've… I know you're just giving me a hard time, but it's… don't downplay the beauty of this thing, it's magnificent. It's not a simple, it's not a weed.
Tarek: So you're saying this is a kind of power move, like… Instead of the most luxurious flower, they chose the most humble one to say, they are that elevated.
DM: The dandelion can go anywhere and do anything, can cross unimaginable distances. That's exactly it, it's not a humble weed. It's magnificent.
Tarek: But the house presumably stays in one place.
DM: Well… I mean, yes, obviously, but… but I… just to say, it's a… It's… it's… you… I… I don't like it when people talk badly about dandelions.
Tarek: Bit of a weed, but… Fair enough.
Edric: They used to cause trouble back home.
Edric: Just… We always had to clear them out of the barley fields.
DM: Yeah, that's… true. They do have a habit of going where they're not wanted.
Edric: I like them, though. Sorry, I'll go back to my food.
DM: Alden falls… silent again. That's his pattern. He usually doesn't have much to say.

before: Txarro: That's probably true.
DM: Was that your favorite part, then? Alden asks.
Txarro: That's always nice. There's something about… tiger that's satisfying. There's a little growl in the back of his throat.

Ayveen: I mean, the teamwork of having a rapid attack, and then a fighter with stamina, my ability to sort of stay back and use ranged spells that kept me from—as a… Kaito says—from getting my clothes dirty, which I just think is a metaphor for experiencing pain. So, I think that it did… was an example of how we've learned to fight together. Because things didn't go as we expected, but we still got through.
DM: Alden nods. Hmm.
after: DM: So unless there's other business or questions that you have for him tonight, he's… he's certainly ready to turn in.
Tarek: He's a… I'm afraid he's a small human.
DM: Yeah. He's sort of a small round human.
Kaito Min: I cast Detect Thoughts.
DM: Tell me… read the description to see, get a… how does it work?

Kaito Min: And what kind of emotions is… is… are attached to this?

DM: I think Kong, like, the last emotional piece there is also a quality of longing, maybe? Maybe it's longing?
Kaito Min: Oh, yeah, but also not… also not, deceptive. Like, he's not, like, lying to us or anything, he's, like, genuinely…
Kaito Min: And also, he's not, does he seem, like, under a spell?

before: Edric: I like them, though. Sorry, I'll go back to my food.

lines: Edric: Edric says, like, a prayer to the Night Queen.
Edric: Fairly extended, you know, watch over us, and… my companions in their sleep, and, you know, please… please let Dandelion House be safe and sound, and… You know, blah blah blah.

before: Edric: You, like… like, Delwath is always just, like, kind of standing around meditating, right? Like, it was not… it's not like.
Kaito Min: Yeah, yeah. Well, I do that.
Edric: Or sitting around meditating.
Kaito Min: Wow.
Kaito Min: I will turn in.
after: DM: You set watches through the night, presumably?
Edric: Yes.
DM: Awesome. Everything passes uneventfully, you're in pretty… even though you're headed deeper into the woods, you're still in relatively civilized territory.
DM: In the morning, you strike camp… and head… onwards. It's a long day's hike. There's a lot of ground to cover. Alden sets a pretty steady pace. Onwards. On and on you go through the day.

DM: The woods get thicker. The… the sort of, background here for us, it's these enormous oaks and ash and elms. I mean, just these huge, huge old trees. You're in a part of the world that must not have been clear-cut for a long, long time, so it must not have been farms for ages and ages.

interactions.title: The pony grows more alert
lines: Edric: How does the pony feel?
DM: Remind me of the pony again? Tell me, like, the pony's… the pony's vibe. What's the… what's the pony's, like, character like? Like… like, like, what if Sam…
Edric: One of Sam's ponies from Lord of the Rings, fine.
DM: Loyal to you. Yeah. Not the bravest, but a little… Yeah, exactly. …badass pony. Yeah. Good.

DM: What you notice is… the pony's not like… resistant or shying away. The pony's just more alert as the day goes on. Like, they… ears are just more… Listening for little sounds. You only hear the wind. You know, but you see the pony listening as the big gust of wind passes far above. It's just more… it's a little bit more locked in. Oh. I didn't name this. I'll reassure.

before: DM: You don't really see much below the canopy. It's quieter and quieter. The wind moving through the dry leaves, almost ready to fall, and some beginning to fall above you, sounds almost like an ocean, like these waves, passing and crashing over you.
DM: These yellow leaves have started to fall down around you here and there. But not much wildlife. Unless, as the day goes on.
DM: Somewhere around noon, Alden says, I don't think we should stop for lunch. I think we should press on so that we get there before dark, and, encourages you to eat as you walk.
Txarro: Fine by me.
Kaito Min: Is, I mean, that's fine. kaito does not like any of this.
after: Kaito Min: I feel like Kaito doesn't like any of this, because Kaito's… not that he likes to eat lunch, but it's just this whole being outside, and it's kind of a little… It's all a little too… something. DM: Soon enough, says Alden. As the day passes on later and the sun starts to sink in the sky… What must be beautiful and low light above the level of the canopy just translates into more and more darkness. The sort of gloom where all the color is drained out of the world down here. And you can see, when you look up, almost like a fiery light reflecting off the changing leaves above you. You can see that looking out, and it's brighter still by the contrast with the gloom down below, but it is… dark down here. And getting darker.
DM: Not far now, says Alden. We are almost there.
Txarro: I will. Okay… summon a flame into my hand with Produce Flame.

Edric: Edric will also, like, sort of… tap their armor, like, on the shoulder or something, and, like, a little light, like, one of the, like, little… almost crown-shaped… starry white just springs up on their shoulder.

interactions.title: Alden’s advice before meeting Hulda
lines: DM: Alden pauses at just about this distance and says to you, Welcome to Dandelion House.
DM: Before we go inside, I need to tell you that… Lord Hulda can be… Difficult sometimes. He needs, at least I've found, a certain amount of… patience, and a certain amount of flattery.
DM: He might not tell you this. But he was born the second son of a lord, and disinherited, and all… I mean, all. All his life! Until this moment, he hasn't had…
DM: This, this is what he's always wanted, all he wanted… was to have a… keep, and his own little patch of the world, and… peasants to work the land, and…
DM: And grass, like… And yes, yes, I, I know, I know, and you know… that Dandelion House is… is going to need some work to get there.

DM: And the forest is gonna need some clearing to get there, and there's… much, much to be done ahead of us. But this is the fulfillment of a dream he's had his entire life, so don't… please… don't… I don't think he'll respond well.
Kaito Min: This place looks beautiful to me. It looks… This looks like when I imagine… A multicolored diamond. And close my eyes, and then I open it here.
DM: That's good, more, yes, more, more of that, yes.
Kaito Min: [garbled] a priceless stone… fit for only… the finest, of all things, just… it's just… it's perfection, it's, it's…
DM: That may actually be too much, but, but, like…
Kaito Min: Dial it back, dial it back, dial it back.
DM: Before you got to the diamond, that was… that was good.
Edric: It's kind of run down, though, right?
((Party discussion of directness and the building’s surroundings.))
DM: Alden… and says, yes, just think of. Think of my conversations with you over the last few days. The way that I've been… polite, and… accommodating. And do that.
DM: Don't worry. It's gonna be great.

before: DM: A little bit, right? Coming over a rise, you can see up ahead, a clearing is opening. You can see it by the quality of light, and Tim, will you switch to the next background for us, please?
Kaito Min: Oh, shit.
DM: And there in front of you is… somewhere between a majestic and decrepit manor house… something that is clearly hundreds of years old.
DM: That seems to be swallowed by the forest, although… maybe not as swallowed by the forest as the forest you've just come through, just.

DM: It's still intact, still in one piece. Even though the windows are gone in many, many of the windows, the stone, the walls are still solid, and even though vines and moss is crawling up it, and in fact the whole back half of it seems almost swallowed by brush and saplings… You get a sense, at least, that the bones are strong. Right? That structurally, it's… solid.
after: DM: Alden leads the way, and through the… bushes and the vines, there is a barely perceptible path to the front door, which is huge iron-banded wooden doors, resting open. And you can tell, just from looking at them that they are unclosable at this point in their life.

DM: And the wood in front of them is warped from the rain, but somehow not totally falling apart. There was… either the open to the elements is recent, or there's some incredible craftsmanship, something more at play here.

Txarro: So before we step through the door to the manor, I'm gonna, like, fall back a little so I'm last in line, so I'm furthest from… Alden, and I will… cast Detect Magic. Just so I have it up when we go into the… Into the… manor.
DM: Nice.
Kaito Min: You're a druid.

DM: Oh, this is such a good question, the… yes, Alden calls out into the house, "Colden! Colden, are you here?" And, "My cousin," is… "Our family has a sort of a sick sense of humor about naming."

DM: Looking over, he sees the pony. "The stables, then," and reaches out a hand to take the reins. What?
DM: Oh, yeah, he certainly acts competent. And Alden says, sensing your hesitation, not to worry, not to worry. We've…

interactions.title: Meeting Hulda upstairs
lines: DM: But in this room, shining through the window like a pillar of light, like a golden spotlight, holds a grim… the lord of Dandelion House: Hulda, who Alden told you is the second son of a minor lord, someone disinherited, resentful his whole life, that he was… You know, not the person ruling over whatever those lands might have been. Is a man in his mid-40s with a grizzled gray beard and a powerful build.

DM: He stands with the sort of bored alertness that you associate with fighting people, the sort of person who has spent a long time standing still and watching and ready for whatever comes. That assessment is cemented… by the sword that he wears at his hip. The impression that you get of that is less of a man prepared for combat in the moment, and more of, this is what the Lord of the Manor does. He wears a sword. He's not armored, but he's wearing… well-worn, but fine clothes.

DM: His sleeves are pulled up to the elbows, and you can see a criss-cross web of… long-healed scars on his forearms and on his face, too. A long cut that interrupts his beard on one side of his face.

DM: Alden announces each of you by name in elaborate style. "My lord, I have the pleasure of presenting…" And one after another introduces, you, nodding and gesturing. His back is still towards you this entire time.
DM: As the sunlight… slowly climbs up his body, the last rays of it shining in through the window, you in the doorway, are already in darkness.

DM: And by the time the long and elaborate introductions have finished, Alden continues on with your bona fides, and the feats that you've done, and the… jobs that you've pulled, the… treasures that you've collected for various people. A sort of a… a summary of everything and the stories that you've shared with him over these last few days on the road. That you thought, probably, were just idle chat around the fire, but realize now maybe he was… collecting and probing exactly for this purpose.
DM: When at last he finishes all of that, the last rays of light disappear from the room. And Hulda, grim… Lord of Dandelion Keep turns to face you.

DM: Looking over you appraisingly, looking over you… Mmm… You've had this sort of look before, this sense of sizing you up. And you've seen it both from prospective employers trying to gauge whether you're really capable of doing the thing they're sending you off to do. And you've also seen that in the looks of people about to draw on you and start a fight, wondering if they can take you.
DM: That sort of ambiguous look from a dangerous person, whether it's an enemy or a friend.
DM: He takes a deep breath and sighs, and says in a not unfriendly way, "Welcome. Welcome, welcome. I know it was a long journey to get here, and I appreciate it. Are you hungry?"
Ayveen: Now that you mention it. We did skip lunch.
DM: Alden… Lead us down to the kitchen, please. Let's find food for everyone.

DM: But there is a bar… next to the sink on one side of the room, a small metal rod about 2 inches in diameter and 6 inches long, affixed into a bracket that is magical.

interactions.title: Hulda’s story and the inheritance bargain
lines: DM: As he sits at the head of the table and begins to dig in and cut his food, he says, you're probably… you're probably curious about the details, you're probably wondering… why you're here?

DM: For almost 30 years, I've been… an adventurer. A sellsword, sometimes, a guard, a… mercenary, a treasure hunter, I've worked for… half the organizations in… Sembara and… even more in Tollen for… wizards and kings and…

DM: I had all sorts of victories and successes. I had all sorts of losses. I made my fortune and lost it a few times over. And what I knew… Hmm… especially after this last one… is that the best days are behind me. And I have never quite come to anything, the…
DM: The party was ending, you know that feeling when a party's breaking up? You can feel that… that the peak has already passed, but… but there you are, still stuck there.

DM: Last winter, there was a… a wyrmling, a young dragon who came down from the… mountains to the north and east of Tollen, and… it was me and a team that I led… who… went out and… killed it and brought the trophy back.

DM: And this surprises the five of you, because you had at least vaguely heard of this, over this last winter. It was sort of a… I mean, it's sort of an unusual thing for a dragon to be that far south and out of the mountains, not that it was a massive ancient thing, but… But it's celebrated, right? It's unusual, remarkable.
DM: He says… I should have been happy. But the truth was…
DM: Everyone I went there with died except for me. And this dragon… had come looking, had come… hungry, it had no territory, it had no… treasure…
DM: I got back to Tollen… and sure, they started writing a song about me.
DM: But I woke up the next morning, and I realized… all of my friends were dead. My purse was… no bigger than it was when I began 3 decades ago.
DM: What was left for me? It was a bitter… it was a difficult day. I was owed more. My whole life. And I hadn't gotten it.
DM: It was a bitter thing to wake up to.

DM: But stranger still, stranger still that later that same day… into the inn I was staying at… eating my lunch, trying my hardest to get ferociously drunk and failing by about noon, into that same inn… walked… an elf, and here's the thing, you… you know Tollen, you know there are strange characters in that city. You know, sometimes when a person says they're a thing, and you know they're not that thing, but you don't quite know what they are. Or who they work for, or what that really means.
DM: He walked into the room, directly over to my table, and sat down across from me.

DM: It's a deed. It's a deed… of inheritance… for… me.

DM: And the elf proceeds to tell me the strangest story that is attested to on the piece of paper in front of him. Now, the five of you looking at this paper can clearly tell this is an ancient, this is an old document. This thing is brittle.
DM: In fact, when he unfolds it, you can see, this is not a person used to taking care of archival documents, because as he unfolds it, you know, little bits of it are, like, flaking off as it goes.
DM: And one should not put a 500-year-old deed in the middle of a dinner table. But there he puts it.
DM: If you read this, you see that it names me.
DM: But this document doesn't just… name… name me by name! It names me by birth. And lists my father's father going back 3 generations.

DM: Not only does it name me by birth and family, it names me by… the deeds I've done… the things that I'm… known for… the accomplishments that I've had, the ones that, even if they didn't bring me money, at least they were known… and remembered. Nay…
DM: I don't know how you all… feel about elves. And he, glances over you without, meeting eye contact.

DM: But as a man nearing 50, it's uncomfortable to me to sit down with someone… 20 times older than me? I don't even know…

DM: He tells me this story. He says… That… hundreds of years ago… when he was young, a young librarian, archivist, I forget what he calls himself exactly, this elf… a man entrusted this contract to him.

DM: And it's sad… entrusted it to him, and, I don't know, paid some sort of unfathomable… some, I don't know how this thing works, like, with elves across centuries. Paid some kind of a sum… For the elf's organization to hold it in trust, for… I don't know, 400 years? And that… It had to be delivered to me… In a specific time, in a specific place, on a specific day. Only after I had done all of the things that it required. And that would be the way that this this elf, or whoever would know my identity. And that I would know it was a… legitimate… deed of inheritance.

DM: He slid it across the table to me, and I read it over, just as you can if you'd like to, and at least at first glance, it appears to be exactly what he says. It deeded to me this… house? This… dandelion? House…

DM: And all the lands surrounding it for dozens of miles. I mean, this is a massive… massive estate, overgrown and in the middle of nowhere, though it may be. Deeded to me this house, and all the treasures therein contained. Including the stores of gold and riches, unspecified in the contract, but alluded to.
DM: On one condition, and in fact, I just gave it away. It turns out it isn't just a deed, but also a contract. I had to sign onto it.

DM: Because down there at the bottom, what it says is that… locked in a room in the basement… is the doom of the house… and that the house will never belong to me… unless I step through the door in the floor… and convinced the man on the other side of it… to bring his long-held treaty to an end.

DM: That was as specific as it is. I've pulled all sorts of jobs for all sorts of people over the years. On the scale of vagueness, this one is probably right in the middle. So I signed. I committed myself to it. My whole life, this is what I've been owed, and finally… I could have it, of course it's worth… negotiating the end to a treaty. Of all the things I've done, how hard can that really be? I came here… and I went through the door… and I met the man on the other side, and I was… unable to convince him.
DM: So I thought that others might be more persuasive than me. And here we are.

DM: In return, for convincing this man to end his treaty, whatever it might be, I'll give you half… of the value… of all of the gold, and all of the coin… and all of the jewels… and all of the wrought jewelry, which is the treasure hoard of this house.

DM: Do you want to pick it up and read it?
Edric: That. I mean, can we see the words from here, or no?
DM: It's written in, yeah, it's written in Sembaran. And if anyone wants to give it an investigation, close read, you're welcome to.

DM: All around you, the walls of the cellar are covered in roots, large and small, some of them massive, some tiny.
after: DM: You inch your way… foot by foot, down the tunnel. You realize after… a little ways… You're not actually crawling on dirt. It feels like the… tunnel itself is… is wood, maybe…
DM: Actually, anyone who wants to, give me a… give me a… investigation. Natural 20. 22. Awesome.

DM: You realize… what you're crawling through… Although the way it's laid out in the background here slightly obscures it. You're crawling through the center of an enormous root. Like, you're not crawling across roots, you're crawling down the middle of some kind of un… fathomably large tree root, maybe with… I mean, who knows how big the diameter is. But you're crawling… coming down through this crack in the center of it.
Kaito Min: That's… so, normal. Probably at the center of the root?
Ayveen: Xylem and phloem?

interactions.title: The door shuts and the deed’s anomaly becomes clear
lines: DM: And I'm gonna say in the moment, as you're in the process of casting the spell… You hear the door close behind you.

DM: And in that same moment, Tarek, you realize the thing about the contract that you didn't quite get in the moment, but now… comes together for you. Unambiguously, unquestionably, that document was 400 years old. It was not a forgery, it was not a fake. It was written… in per… perfectly contemporary Sembaran.
Tarek: Oh… So there's just something that doesn't add up here.
Txarro: Why didn't he take it to the Philosopher's Guild? I mean, come on.

before: Kaito Min: If this was a bone, we would be wet right now.
DM: You crawl further and further, and the scant light behind you dwindles.
Txarro: I'm gonna summon…
Edric: I'm gonna summon a light, too. I'm not… This darkness thing.
DM: Yeah, why… just before… the light dwindles entirely…
after: Edric: Did you just hear the door closed?
Ayveen: Yes.
Tarek: Guys, there's something that doesn't add up here.
Txarro: Yeah, I told you.
Edric: Heyo!
